solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I have joined in support, receiving something to chew over

indicators.note: receiving means the first pieces take another piece into their middle

parts.note: taken as written
a tee is the little peg that supports a golf ball

indicators.note: over, after the thing to chew, says that word is turned round

parts.note: cud is what a cow brings up to chew again

explanation.surface: Someone describes taking up membership while being propped up and given food for thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the cud round; 'receiving' sets it between IN and the golf tee. The definition is what a new recruit would say of themselves, standing for that person.
explanation.definitionFit: A recruit newly admitted to a group could say these words of themselves, so the phrase stands for that person.

clue.text: Some claim pedestrians get in the way

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Walkers are accused of obstructing traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: To obstruct or hinder someone's progress is to block their path.

clue.text: Expert sort of radio operative

parts.note: DAB is digital audio broadcasting, a kind of radio
a hand is a worker or operative

explanation.surface: A skilled kind of wireless operator.
explanation.definitionFit: A dab hand is a British idiom for someone highly skilled at something.

clue.text: By using brain, convention latches on to cold beer that's brewed

indicators.note: latches on to means the word for convention attaches itself after the other pieces

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: brewed means the letters of beer are stirred into a new order

parts.note: a rally is a mass gathering or convention

explanation.surface: Conference-goers cleverly seize on chilled home-made beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's brewed' scrambles the beer, and 'latches on to' puts the rally at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting intellectually, through the mind rather than feeling, is acting with the brain.

clue.text: Coppers stride out with pride in force

indicators.note: out means the letters of coppers stride are put out of order

explanation.surface: Police officers march out, proud of their constabulary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'force' looks like strength but means a body such as a police force or army unit.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase names the morale and loyalty shared by members of a group or unit.

clue.text: Doctor joins boat for capital

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a military doctor
a scow is a flat-bottomed boat

explanation.surface: A medic climbs aboard a vessel bound for a nation's chief city.
explanation.definitionFit: Moscow is the capital city of Russia, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Regretful woman is oppressed by sacred text

indicators.note: in a down clue, oppressed by means is sits underneath the sacred text

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A sorrowful woman is weighed down by scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss Otis Regrets is a Cole Porter song in which Miss Otis regrets she cannot lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of the Cole Porter song is a lady sending her regrets.

clue.text: Man dealing with one piece of bread

parts.note: a chap is a man
at means busy with, as in hard at it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A fellow handling a single slice of a loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: This unleavened Indian flatbread is cooked on a griddle, one round at a time.

clue.text: Small piece of fowl split between two?

definitions.text: Small piece of fowl split between two?

parts.words: Small piece of fowl split between two?
parts.note: the forked bone of a chicken is pulled apart by two people, the one with the larger piece making a wish

explanation.surface: A tiny portion of poultry is shared by a pair of diners.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as two people sharing a scrap of meat, but the split is the custom of snapping the bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The forked breastbone of a bird is broken by two people after a meal, and the longer piece gets the wish.

clue.text: Local people's unusually big heads

indicators.note: heads means the first letter of each of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: Folk in the neighbourhood have strangely large skulls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' looks like an adjective describing the people, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang your local is the neighbourhood drinking house you regularly use.

clue.text: Politicians resolve to dishearten ordinary people, — and nearly succeeded later

indicators.note: to dishearten the word resolve is to take out all its middle, leaving its ends

parts.note: the public are ordinary people in general

indicators.note: nearly means the word and loses its last letter

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: A political scheme to demoralise the masses almost works later on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to dishearten' leaves RE from resolve; 'nearly' cuts and to AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a party such as the US Republican Party are politicians; the plural matches.

clue.text: Encouraging line enclosed by speculator, one after money

indicators.note: enclosed by means the first pieces sit inside the word for speculator

parts.note: a better is one who bets, a speculator
egging on is urging or encouraging

explanation.surface: A gambler slips a cheering note to someone chasing cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one after money' is a letter, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A written appeal asking for funds or donations is chasing cash.

clue.text: Failure to win game that's raised to shut one out

definitions.text: that's raised to shut one out

parts.note: a draw is a match neither side wins
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A tied match in some sport is lifted to exclude a player.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle's hinged crossing over a moat is hoisted to keep attackers from entering.

clue.text: Post spread by word of mouth

indicators.note: by word of mouth says the word is heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: jam is a fruit spread for bread

explanation.surface: A message is passed around orally rather than in writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' and 'spread' look like a message being circulated; the B is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: The upright side piece of a door or window frame is a kind of post.

clue.text: Not hindered, as forgetful picnickers may be?

definitions.meaning: picnickers who left their basket behind would be without a hamper

explanation.surface: Free to move, as people who forgot their picnic basket might be.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as UN-HAMPERED: lacking a hamper, a picnic basket.
explanation.definitionFit: Unimpeded and free, and comically also lacking the wicker basket of food.

clue.text: I had been concerned, short of energy, for a way to prove myself

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

indicators.note: short of means a letter is missing from the word for been concerned

parts.note: to have cared is to have been concerned
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone worried, lacking vigour, about how to establish their worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prove myself' suggests proving one's worth, but here it means proving who one is.
explanation.definitionFit: An identity card is a document showing who the holder is, proving identity.

clue.text: Poor innings: one's out for 9

indicators.note: a poor innings is badly played, so its letters are put in a bad order

explanation.surface: A cricket batter's weak effort: dismissed for only nine runs.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' refers to 9 across, PUB; 'out' means hung outside, not dismissed at cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted board hangs outside a British drinking house to advertise it, the answer to 9.

clue.text: Behave outrageously, seeing river bed higher

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
pit is British slang for bed
up means higher

explanation.surface: Someone acts wildly on seeing a riverbed rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'river bed' reads as one thing, the floor of a river; it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to overact or behave in an exaggerated, theatrical way.

clue.text: Pure English penned by member of church — only the first article appears

indicators.note: the word for the churchgoer ends in a second article, an, which is dropped so only the first a stays
penned by means held inside the word for the church member

parts.note: an Anglican belongs to the Church of England

explanation.surface: Untainted English is written by a churchgoer, with a grammar note about articles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' puts E inside ANGLICAN to give ANGELICAN; dropping its final AN leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something like an angel is innocent and good, so the adjective means pure.

clue.text: Bigger kitchen utensil announced

indicators.note: announced means the word is spoken aloud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a grater is a kitchen tool for shredding cheese

explanation.surface: A larger cooking tool has been declared.
explanation.definitionFit: Larger in size or amount is a direct synonym of the comparative adjective.

clue.text: Take holiday somewhere near Indian state

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
way, as in round our way, means the area somewhere near a place

explanation.surface: A traveller plans a break near a region of India.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the pieces as a phrase, 'Goa way', and it means somewhere near Goa.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave home for a trip or vacation is an everyday idiom for taking a holiday.

clue.text: In car boot, half empty, a broken tumbler

indicators.note: broken means the letters of car and the trimmed boot are smashed into a new order
half empty means the pair of inner letters in boot is only half cleared out, so one of them remains

explanation.surface: A smashed drinking glass lies in a car's luggage space, which is partly empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tumbler' looks like a glass but is a gymnast. 'half empty' leaves one of the two inner letters of the boot, like half-hearted; 'broken' scrambles the rest, with A in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who does somersaults and flips is a gymnast who tumbles.

clue.text: An irrational boss comes across as foolish

indicators.note: comes across means the word for boss spans the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a stud is a boss, a raised knob or rivet head
pi is an irrational number

explanation.surface: An unreasonable manager seems silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' looks like a manager, but it means a knob or rivet head, STUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking intelligence or good sense is a direct synonym of senseless.

clue.text: Huntsman's strip

definitions.meaning: John ... was the famous Cumbrian huntsman of the song D'ye ken John ...
to strip a fruit is to remove its skin

explanation.surface: A hunter's undressing.
explanation.definitionFit: John Peel was a celebrated huntsman, and removing skin from fruit is a synonym of strip.

clue.text: An independent thinker, like Ariel finally?

definitions.meaning: a person who lives and thinks unconstrained by convention
Ariel is the sprite in Shakespeare's The Tempest, released from Prospero's service at the end

explanation.surface: An original mind, compared with the Tempest's sprite at the play's close.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: Ariel, a spirit, is liberated at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonconformist is described by the idiom, and Ariel is literally a spirit set at liberty.

clue.text: Request enjoyment? Not certainly

indicators.note: Not means the word for certainly is left out of the word for enjoyment

parts.note: pleasure is enjoyment
sure means certainly

explanation.surface: Someone asks for some fun, then hesitates and is unsure.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest appeal or entreaty is a synonym of request.

clue.text: Entire rota is to be changed, you can bet on it

parts.note: entire means total

indicators.note: to be changed means the letters of rota is are rearranged

explanation.surface: A whole duty schedule must be redrawn, and that's a sure thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you can bet on it' looks like the idiom for certainty; it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tote is a pool-betting machine at racecourses where wagers are placed and odds computed.

clue.text: Dance, nothing to swell blood pressure

indicators.note: to swell means a letter fills out the abbreviation from inside

parts.note: BP is the medical abbreviation for blood pressure
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Dancing will not raise your blood pressure at all.
explanation.definitionFit: To bop is to dance energetically to pop music, an informal synonym.

clue.text: A doctor in residence perhaps pulled back hospital screen

indicators.note: pulled back means the pieces before it are read in reverse order

parts.note: up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A resident doctor draws back a curtain round a hospital bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled back' reverses the first three pieces only; H for hospital follows. Being up means in residence at a university.
explanation.definitionFit: In parts of South Asia, a curtain or practice secluding women from view is a screen.

clue.text: Came earlier and hunted food

definitions.meaning: to come before something in time
an animal that stalked and killed its prey

explanation.surface: Arrived before and went foraging for something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Antedated something in time, and also preyed upon other animals for food.
